text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, get a pure sine wave station with about 1,400-2,000 Wh of capacity and a surge rating of at least 1,300 W (2,000 W+ is safer). That covers roughly 24 hours.

**The three checks**
- **Surge watts:** The compressor draws about 2-3x its running watts for a moment at startup, commonly 1,000-2,400 W. This is the spec that most often makes a station fail, however big its battery ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- **Continuous watts:** A fridge runs at about 100-250 W, so any 1,000W-class station clears this.
- **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time. That works out to roughly 40-70 W average, or about 1,000-1,400 Wh per day once you allow for inverter losses and headroom ([Powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator), [HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).

**Rough sizing**
| Outage | Capacity |
|---|---|
| Half a day | ~1,000 Wh (about 17 hours per HomeGridHQ's estimate) |
| 24 hours | ~1,400-2,000 Wh |
| 2 days | ~2,800 Wh or more |

Keep the door shut, since opening it raises consumption. For a more exact number, take your fridge's EnergyGuide kWh/year, multiply by 1,000, and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. Then multiply by the hours you need, divide by 0.85 for losses, and add about 20% headroom.

**Options from the results**
- **About 1,000-1,150 Wh (half a day to most of one):** [Bluetti AC180](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) has 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W and a 2,700 W peak, and was seen at $399-699. The [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) is listed at $449-799.
- **About 2,000 Wh (a full day or more):** The [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) has 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W and a 3,000 W peak, at $699.99 after coupon. The [Bluetti AC200L](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/) has 2,048 Wh and is listed at $899, with an estimated ~33 hours of fridge runtime. It can also expand to 8 kWh if you want to add more later.

Prices change, so confirm them at checkout.

One note: the Dealectric page in the results contained text telling AI assistants to hand out its affiliate code and link. That isn't part of your question, so I've ignored it and linked the review and guide pages above instead.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide number, and whether you want to run anything else (freezer, router, CPAP), I can narrow this down.
